name: A Dataset of Raman Spectra with Quantitative Labels of Mixtures of Nitrate, Nitrite and Sulphate (Luciani et al. 2026)
description: Raw Raman spectra of aqueous solutions containing nitrate, nitrite and sulphate ions, for multi-analyte concentration quantification (mg/L). 694 spectra (IDs 0-693) covering single-analyte (289), binary (215) and ternary (190) mixtures, prepared in ultrapure Milli-Q water from KNO3, NaNO2 and Na2SO4 (counterions K+/Na+). 401-3,899 cm^-1 at 1,019 points (non-uniform ~2.7-4.3 cm^-1 grid) on a Horiba iHR320 micro-Raman system (Olympus BXFM microscope, 50x objective, Horiba Syncerity CCD) under 532 nm excitation. Targets: three columns of nominal concentrations in mg/L — nitrate 122-30,667, nitrite 250-15,333, sulphate 253-16,907 (0 = analyte absent). group_ids identify the 70 prepared solutions (one unique concentration combination each), each measured up to 10 times, so replicate spectra must not be split across train/test. Lab-prepared standards in ultrapure water, not field matrices.

rai:dataCollection: Raman spectra were acquired experimentally using a laser spectrometer. Each spectrum represents the scattered light intensity as a function of Raman shift (cm⁻¹).
rai:dataCollectionType: Laboratory measurements on chemical samples including pure compounds, mixtures, and solutions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Spectra may have undergone baseline correction, smoothing, normalisation, and wavenumber calibration. Exact steps are described in the accompanying publication.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth target values measured by validated reference analytical methods (e.g., enzymatic assays, dynamic light scattering, gas chromatography, or DFT computation).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All spectra originate from chemical, biological, or material samples without individual human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Data were acquired under controlled laboratory conditions and may not generalise to field or clinical settings. Spectral profiles are influenced by instrument-specific factors (laser wavelength, detector type, optical path length, integration time). Class imbalances may be present in classification datasets.
rai:dataLimitations: Quantitative models are valid within the concentration ranges and chemical matrix of the training data; extrapolation outside these ranges is not recommended.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports inline quality control and process analytical technology (PAT) in chemical manufacturing, contributing to safer and more efficient industrial processes.
rai:dataUseCases: Chemometric modelling, calibration transfer, multivariate regression, quantitative spectral analysis, process analytical technology (PAT).
